efficacy.model: Healthy cynomolgus monkey (4- and 8-week repeat-dose toxicology studies, cotadutide)

efficacy.model: Healthy cynomolgus monkey (4- and 8-week repeat-dose toxicology studies, cotadutide)
efficacy.note: Cotadutide cut weight 2.1 kg vs placebo over 41 days in T2D patients (co-primary met); the monkey's weight prediction held, direction only.
efficacy.short: Weight co-primary met; monkey had no glucose arm
efficacy.quote: In the ITT population, reduction in bodyweight was significantly greater with MEDI0382 than with placebo (LS mean -3·84 kg [90% CI -4·55 to -3·12] vs -1·70 kg [-2·40 to -1·01] and mean difference of 2·14 kg [-3·13 to -1·31]; p=0·0008).
efficacy.confidence_note: Patient side abstract-level (Lancet paywalled); model side full text. Monkey doses (30-100 ug/kg/d) were ~10-40x the human 200 ug/day on a per-kg basis, so no magnitude can be ratioed.
efficacy.reason: Weight loss translated; glucose not monkey-predicted
efficacy.judgement: Paired by the drafter: Henderson 2016 reported dose-dependent weight loss in healthy monkeys dosed with cotadutide itself and 'no notable changes in plasma glucose or insulin'; Ambery 2018 met both co-primaries (weight and MMTT glucose AUC) vs placebo. Same, direction only, because the trial's weight co-primary moved as the monkey said. Partial because the monkey, being non-diabetic, predicted nothing about glucose, and the superiority over a GLP-1R agonist that motivated the class did not hold at 54 weeks (NCT03235050: cotadutide 300 ug vs liraglutide 1.8 mg weight p=0.357, per the draft's dio-mouse judgement). Registry results posted 2019-04-05, after the 2018-06-23 online date, so the year is 2018.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of body weight vs placebo; monkeys lost up to ~20 % in 8 weeks at 27 nmol/kg/d, patients 3.8 kg (~4 %) in 41 days at <=200 ug/day, doses not matched

safety.model: Healthy cynomolgus monkey (4- and 8-week repeat-dose toxicology studies, cotadutide)
safety.note: Cotadutide-dosed monkeys, a species that vomits, showed no adverse clinical signs or vomiting at 8-27 nmol/kg/d; one 27 nmol/kg animal was killed for weight loss.
safety.short: No vomiting or clinical signs in monkeys
safety.quote: Bodyweight loss was not associated with any adverse clinical signs or vomiting in monkeys
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5129521); quote is the opening clause of a longer sentence that goes on to describe one female at 27 nmol/kg/d killed on day 36 for poor clinical condition attributed to ~20 % weight loss.
safety.judgement: Opening untested entry. Unlike the DIO mouse, the monkey can show emesis, so this is a stated negative safety prediction in a capable species; the same paper also calls the receptor balance 'optimal for both glycaemic control and safety'.

safety.model: Healthy cynomolgus monkey (4- and 8-week repeat-dose toxicology studies, cotadutide)
safety.note: Phase 2a: GI disorders in 72 % of cotadutide patients vs 40 % on placebo, 3 of 25 stopped for adverse events; monkeys showed none.
safety.short: Monkeys clean; 72 % GI disorders in patients
safety.quote: gastrointestinal disorders (18 [72%] vs 13 [40%]) and decreased appetite (five [20%] vs none) occurred more frequently with MEDI0382 than placebo.
safety.confidence_note: Patient side abstract-level (PubMed abstract via efetch; Lancet paywalled), which gives GI disorders as a group, not vomiting alone; the vomiting rate comes in the 2020 strengthening entry. Model side full text.
safety.judgement: Paired by the drafter: Henderson 2016 stated, for cotadutide itself in a species that can vomit, that weight loss 'was not associated with any adverse clinical signs or vomiting'; Ambery 2018 found GI disorders in 72 % vs 40 % and all four phase 2a discontinuations were for adverse events. A stated prediction of no GI harm in a capable species, contradicted in patients, is contra on this track (the dio-mouse track stays untested on this harm because a mouse cannot vomit, and the GI dose ceiling is already counted in that track's dose cell). The monkey toxicology doses were far above the clinical dose, which makes the miss worse, not better. Not 'opposite' in magnitude: that term is for a predicted harm that never appeared; here the model predicted absence. Registry results (NCT02548585) posted 2019-04-05, after the 2018-06-23 online date.
safety.magnitude_basis: GI disorders 72 % vs 40 % placebo (phase 2a, n=25 vs 26) against a stated absence of adverse clinical signs or vomiting in monkeys at 30-100 ug/kg/d; no rate to ratio

safety.model: Healthy cynomolgus monkey (4- and 8-week repeat-dose toxicology studies, cotadutide)
safety.note: 54-week phase 2b (n=834): nausea 35 % and vomiting 17 % with cotadutide, more than placebo or liraglutide. Vomiting itself, the harm the monkey denied.
safety.quote: The most common adverse events with cotadutide (nausea, 35%; vomiting, 17%) decreased over time.
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC8247525). Vomiting rate is pooled across 100-300 ug doses; the paper also states cotadutide had more GI disorders than placebo and liraglutide.
safety.judgement: Strengthens the 2018 contra with the specific harm the monkey study named. Year 2020 because the trial's registry results (NCT03235050) posted 2020-07-20, before the 2021-05-20 online publication that carries the quotable sentence (rule 6: earliest public date); the registry AE table lists vomiting counts but no sentence.
safety.magnitude_basis: vomiting 17 %, nausea 35 % of cotadutide-treated T2D patients over 54 weeks vs none stated in monkeys; no rate to ratio

engagement.model: Human GLP-1 + glucagon co-infusion challenge (overweight volunteers without diabetes)
engagement.note: 19 days of SAR425899 under calorie restriction: adjusted sleeping metabolic rate fell less than placebo (p=0.002), fat oxidation rose, but 24-h EE did not differ.
engagement.short: Adjusted SMR held up; 24-h EE unchanged
engagement.quote: SAR425899 led to reduced selective metabolic adaptation and increased lipid oxidation, which are believed to be beneficial for weight loss and weight-loss maintenance.
engagement.confidence_note: Read from the PMC author manuscript (PMC9881753); published abstract quoted. n=35 healthy adults with overweight/obesity (not T2D patients), -1000 kcal/day diet, SAR425899 0.06-0.2 mg/day; NCT03376802 has no posted results.
engagement.reason: Adjusted SMR held up; 24-h EE unchanged
engagement.judgement: Paired by the drafter: the co-infusion model's readout is energy expenditure, and Corbin 2023 is the only member trial that measured it by whole-room calorimetry. Scored same with partial: the primary endpoint (sleeping metabolic rate adjusted for lean and fat mass) fell less with SAR425899 than placebo, i.e. relatively higher as the infusion predicted, but absolute 24-hour energy expenditure was not different, so the +53 kcal/day resting-EE prediction did not show as a raw increase. Healthy volunteers count for engagement. Not contra because the pre-specified primary moved in the predicted direction. Corbin's introduction says the human impact of glucagon-receptor-driven EE 'is unclear' and does not set its result beside Tan or Cegla, so comparison_stated is false.
engagement.magnitude_basis: co-infusion: resting EE up (+53 kcal/day at subanorectic doses, Cegla 2014); SAR425899: body-composition-adjusted sleeping metabolic rate fell less than placebo (p=0.002), 24-h EE not different

Cotadutide cynomolgus monkey engagement cell: the monkey readouts (weight, food intake, fasting glucose/insulin) are the same downstream ones carried in its efficacy cell; not duplicated.

Non-human-primate GCGR PET occupancy model (Eriksson 2019, 10.1038/s41598-019-51530-0): run with an acylated glucagon mono-agonist (1-GCG), not a member; the human PET follow-up (Eriksson 2020) is already in the draft's dio-mouse engagement cell.

Pancreatic GLP1R PET density as a patient-level predictor (Eriksson 2021, 10.2967/jnumed.121.262506): n=7 on SAR425899 'all responded ... regardless of exhibiting a wide range of GLP1R density'; no prediction stated beforehand and too thin to open a patient-level track.

Cotadutide nausea exposure-response Markov model (10.1002/psp4.13194, 2024) and CKD PK/PD model (10.1002/bcp.70093, 2025): fitted to pooled clinical data to optimise titration / describe UACR, no prediction set against a later patient result; the CKD model is outside the T2D context.
4GI dose cell: the 2024 abstract's glucose-lowering plateau near 200 ug is a dose-response retrodiction with no stated human exposure target; not scored.

In-vitro cell lines, beta-cell GSIS and primary hepatocyte HGO assays (Henderson 2016; Bosch 2021 potency inputs): potency assays with no direct patient comparison; their only patient-facing use is as inputs to the qsp-4gi track.
ob/ob + AMLN-diet NASH mouse and primary human hepatocytes for cotadutide (Boland 2020, Nat Metab): a NASH model outside the T2D context; its patient comparison is the NASH programme, not T2D.
Human GCGR loss-of-function genetics (Mahvash disease, P86S): no comparison with any member drug found.

Efinopegdutide (HM12525A/JNJ-64565111), pegapamodutide (LY2944876/OPK-88003/TT-401) and MK-8521 member-specific models: Europe PMC searches returned reviews only, no primary preclinical paper to open a track on; MK-8521's own model is Pocai 2009, already the dio-mouse track.

Human GLP-1 + glucagon co-infusion dose and safety cells: subanorectic infusion doses set no human exposure target, and the acute glucagon hyperglycaemia the infusion showed is a mechanism note, not a stated harm prediction for a dual agonist.
